title: A deactivated term still dates new invoices for customers who keep it
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a new term of the shop's own for this test, term A, due 14 days after the invoice date.
  • Create work order 1 for this test, complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done), for a customer on term A.
  • Then deactivate term A.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1's Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  3. Click Create Invoice.
  4. Open the printed invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice preview shows.

Step 2:

  • The due date reads Oct 19, 2026 (Oct 5 + 14 days).

Step 3:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 4:

  • The printed invoice shows term A's plain name (no "(Inactive)") and the due date Oct 19, 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11674 (Story 5, New Customer and Edit Customer), story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-E1: “A deactivated term still dates invoices and vendor invoices for the customers and vendors that keep it.”
  • S5-R8: “The customer card's "Credit term" shows "{name} (Inactive)" for a deactivated term. Invoices and printed documents show the plain name.”
